feature: Fix a pop: seeded, single-location plosive/pop attenuation (service/deplosive.py, plugin/deplosive.js)

python_tests.note: Failures reproduce only under this session's substitute Python 3.10 environment (a borrowed env from a sibling project, not the product's real work/service-env). All are pre-existing and unrelated to this feature: service/stage_cache.py's digest_file() uses hashlib.file_digest(), added in Python 3.11, so every test that submits a /v1/jobs job fails with AttributeError under 3.10. Full-suite pass has not been re-confirmed against the real Python 3.12 work/service-env in this session.

real_audio_regression: tests/test_deplosive.py's test_real_audio_three_measured_plosives_are_each_reduced_by_at_least_half re-validates the same function against the three real plosives measured during investigation (61-83% peak reduction, 68-82% RMS reduction each); skipped automatically if that external fixture is not present on the machine running tests.

bugs_found_and_fixed_before_native_confi.bug: plugin/local-api.js's endpoint allow-list regex did not include /v1/deplosive or the /v1/assets/{id}/download route added for this feature, so every click of Fix a pop failed immediately with 'Unexpected local service endpoint.' before reaching the service at all.
bugs_found_and_fixed_before_native_confi.fix: Added both routes to the allow-list regex.
bugs_found_and_fixed_before_native_confi.regression_test: tests/local-api.test.cjs: 'deplosive and asset-download routes are allowed (regression for "Unexpected local service endpoint")'

bugs_found_and_fixed_before_native_confi.bug: The attenuated clip's output WAV was written to fs.getTemporaryFolder(), imported, and placed on the timeline as that clip's live media reference -- then the entire temporary folder (including that same file) was deleted in run()'s finally block right after placement. The fix appeared to work (Premiere's cached/preview playback masked it) but the clip's actual backing file was gone. The fixed clip's new path was also never recorded on context.dialoguePaths, so a second Fix a pop on that same clip could not recognize it as a valid target.
bugs_found_and_fixed_before_native_confi.fix: Fixed clips now write to a persistent, user-chosen folder (asked once per clone via fs.getFolder(), reused for later fixes in the same session, matching per-clip.js/premiere.js's existing convention for every other stem output). Only the throwaway isolated-render export is deleted after upload. context.dialoguePaths is appended with the new path after each successful fix. Filenames use a random suffix, not just Date.now(), after a same-millisecond collision surfaced while testing this fix.
regression_tests: tests/deplosive.test.cjs: 'regression: the fixed clip's output file is never deleted (it is the timeline clip's live media from here on)'
tests/deplosive.test.cjs: 'regression: the fixed clip is recognized as fixable again on a second run (context.dialoguePaths includes its new path)'

native_premiere_acceptance: outstanding for Fix a pop specifically; user reported the endpoint-allowlist bug and the apparent-success/second-run bug from real usage before either fix above, and has not yet confirmed the corrected version
deferred: fully automatic plosive detection (deliberately out of scope; see service/deplosive.py's module docstring -- simple energy-ratio detection could not reliably distinguish the real, human-flagged pop from ordinary loud speech in the validation file)
